messages.subject: sim.cross output: data vs. truegeno
parts:
Hi,

I do not fully understand the output of sim.cross and have not found
any documentation on the following:

When, for example, I run the example of inbreeding in sim.cross, i.e.

ril <- sim.cross(themap, n.ind=256, type="ri8sib", founderGeno=pg),

i obtain, amongst other, a list of name "geno". Within this list there
are
four lists called "data", "map", "errors" and "truegeno". What is
"data"
and "truegeno" and what is the difference? Is it just a different
coding
of the genotypes? If the parents were original 0/1
SNP data how do I obtain an RI with 0/1 data again?

Thanks a lot for any comments!

messages.author: 844c598accb0c0d0
messages.subject: Re: sim.cross output: data vs. truegeno
parts:
Just FYI for anyone who encountered the same problem:

In order to obtain 0/1 marker data for RIL I did the following:
(note that pg only has one chromosome in this example)

ril = sim.cross(themap, n.ind=1, type="ri8sib", founderGeno=pg)
cross.order= pg[[1]][,ril$cross[1,]]
ril.marker = cross.order[,1]*2^0
+cross.order[,2]*2^1
+cross.order[,3]*2^2
+cross.order[,4]*2^3
+cross.order[,5]*2^4
+cross.order[,6]*2^5
+cross.order[,7]*2^6
+cross.order[,8]*2^7
ril.marker = as.numeric(ril.marker == ril$geno[[1]]$data[1,])

Maybe there is a more straight forward way to do it.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] sim.cross output: data vs. truegeno
parts:
The simulation of 8-way RIL data in R/qtl is still "developmental". We're still working out how best to encode the data, and so aspects of this are particularly awkward at the moment. Nevertheless..

In the geno portion of the output of sim.cross for type="ri8sib",

data = matrix of snp genotypes with special encoding that indicates compatibility with founder strains' genotypes
truegeno = matrix of underlying 'true' genotypes (coded 1-8, indicating the 8 founder strains)

In the absence of genotyping errors or missing data, the simplest approach to get the SNP genotypes would be to pull out the founders' SNPs using the 'truegeno' information, as follows:

set.seed(85238087)
map <- sim.map(50, n.mar=26, eq.spacing=TRUE, include.x=FALSE)
fsnps <- simFounderSnps(map, n.str="8")
x <- sim.cross(map, n.ind=10, type="ri8sib", founderGeno=fsnps)

trueg <- x$geno[[1]]$truegeno
snpg <- trueg
for(i in 1:nrow(trueg))
for(j in 1:ncol(trueg))
snpg[i,j] <- fsnps[[1]][j,trueg[i,j]]


With potential errors or missing data, it's best to use the 'data' component (which includes simulated errors and missing data). In this case, look at whether the data are compatible with the "first" strain, and then pull out the SNP genotype for that strain.

sameas1 <- x$geno[[1]]$data %% 2
sameas1[is.na(sameas1)] <- 0
snpg2 <- sameas1
for(i in 1:nrow(sameas1)) {
for(j in 1:ncol(sameas1)) {
if(sameas1[i,j])
snpg2[i,j] <- fsnps[[1]][j,x$cross[i,1]]
else
snpg2[i,j] <- 1-fsnps[[1]][j,x$cross[i,1]]
}
}
snpg2[is.na(x$geno[[1]]$data)] <- NA

karl
